reason: The only available action appears to prepare a body-free section for the warming test.
expectation: I expect the cold enclosure to expose or separate a test section while preserving the specimen; the exact preparation is unclear.

effect: The body-free test section is separated while the specimen and neighboring ice remain sealed and cold, so it is ready for the warming test.
reaction: I’m curious what the band will lose as it warms.
reason: The temperature stage is the only available gameplay action and seems suited to testing how warming changes the layer.
expectation: I expect the stage to warm the section and reveal changes in the band, though I don’t know what those changes will be.

effect: The test showed that material can move within the layer at minus 30 even while the ice looks solid. Preserving the specimen requires keeping its surrounding layer colder as well.
reaction: I was surprised that changes began so far below ordinary melting temperature.

mostWorthwhile.text: The warming test was most worthwhile because it showed why preserving the body’s outline alone is not enough; its surroundings can change too.

leastWorthwhile.text: Separating the test section was necessary but less engaging on its own.

surprise.text: Fine pockets changed and material moved between grains at minus 30 while the section still looked solid.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary: the section was taken away from the body, then tested on the temperature stage. Both were the only gameplay options offered at their respective steps.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the specimen and its surrounding ice are kept cold for the journey home; the test made that challenge more concrete.
